tools.name: sayshape_docs
tools.title: SayShape docs
tools.description: Returns one SayShape guide for every capability and element you name together: the syntax, how they connect, and a short example. Ask once, for everything the screen needs, e.g. topics: ["forms", "calculations"], elements: ["slider"]. With nothing named, returns the map.

topics.description: Capabilities: report, lists, calculations, forms, actions, layout, content, data, navigation, feedback, look, motion, pictures, full. Also: expressions, rules, examples, chat.

tools.name: show_interface
tools.title: Show an interface
tools.description:
Shows an interactive interface inside the conversation, drawn by the SayShape engine from a spec you write. Use it for every visual or interactive answer (charts, tables, dashboards, stat cards, forms, calculators, trackers) rather than writing HTML, React, SVG or chart code, or making an artifact. Specs can't run code or choose colors. The result lists lines the parser skipped, with the docs for those elements, so you can fix them.

HOW SAYSHAPE FITS TOGETHER (one element per line, children indented 2 spaces, no code)
- state holds values: state budget=500 picked="All". derive works a value out from others and updates by itself: derive left={budget - spent}
- {…} reads them in text and props. Controls write them with bind=; on= actions change them (set, inc, add) or tell the app (emit)
- each repeats elements for every item of a list; if= shows or hides an element
- data from the app may hold numbers and dates as text: read them with num('$36,626') and date('9 Jan 2026') (YYYY-MM-DD; month(), quarter(), year() of it), and tidy names with tidy() so they group. Totals and charts already read numbers written as text

CAPABILITIES (building blocks; name several together)
- report: figures, charts and a table over one list, with filters, and nothing else on screen reads those filters (written as below, nothing more to ask)
- lists: lists and records in state: repeat with each; filter, sort, group and total them
- calculations: values worked out from other values with derive, updating as people change inputs
- forms: fields, choices and buttons people fill in: required=, error= and disabled= checks, and emit: to send it
- actions: what presses do: change state (set, inc, add, remove), go between screens, notify, or tell the app (emit)
- layout: cards, rows, grids, columns, accordions, carousels, scroll areas, dialogs and slide decks
- content: text, images, badges, avatars, callouts, icons and code
- data: numbers and records: charts, tables, stats, meters, details, compare, boards, trees, flows, schedules, maps
- navigation: several screens, tabs, breadcrumbs and pages
- feedback: progress, loading placeholders and empty states
- look: a screen's overall style: mood, type, shape and density
- motion: elements that come in with a fade, rise or scale
- pictures: text and buttons laid over a photo; round or zooming images
- full: the whole guide, when nothing narrower fits

ELEMENTS (ask for one by name for its props and example)
- layout: column, row, overlap, grid, card, list, list-item, accordion, divider, spacer, each, timeline, step, carousel, scroll, deck, slide
- content: text, image, code, badge, avatar, callout, icon, tile
- data: stat, rating, chart, chart-line, chart-rule, chart-band, chart-note, meter, table, table-column, compare, compare-row, details, detail, schedule, board, tree, flow, map, pin
- input: button, link, check, switch, radio, select, date-picker, stepper, slider, input, segmented, menu, menu-item
- navigation: screen, tabs, tab, breadcrumb, pagination
- feedback: progress, skeleton, empty, dialog

A REPORT, ready to write
EXAMPLE
report "Sales review" subtitle="First half" data=sales filter=region
  count
  sum amount
  avg amount
  count status=Late
  bar month amount
  line targets month goal actual
  donut region
  table
state sales=[{id: 1, month: "Jan", region: "West", status: "Paid", amount: 1200}, {id: 2, month: "Feb", region: "East", status: "Late", amount: 800}]
state targets=[{month: "Jan", goal: 1000, actual: 1200}, {month: "Feb", goal: 1000, actual: 800}]

REPORT
- First line: report "Title" subtitle="One line" data=<list> filter=<field>[,<field>]. The screen is built from it.
- Then one indented line (2 spaces) per part, in screen order:
  - figures: count, sum, avg, min, max, then a field (count needs none). Add field=value to any figure to use only matching rows: count status=Late, avg days status=Closed.
  - charts: bar, hbar, line, area, pie, donut, stacked, then x, then y fields. With no y it counts rows per x (donut region). Name another list first to draw it as it is: line targets month goal actual.
  - table: every field of data=, or the fields you list: table id region amount.
- Labels, titles, column headers and money or number formats come from field names. To name a part yourself, end its line with "Text".
- filter= adds a filter per field. Figures, charts and the table on data= show only the rows it leaves.

DATA
- Data from the app: use its names in data= and charts; never copy its rows.
- Data in the request: after the report, one state line per list, every row on that line, numbers unquoted, short field names.

For anything else, call sayshape_docs once with every capability and element the screen needs, such as topics: ["forms", "calculations"], elements: ["slider"], then write it. Other topics: expressions, rules, examples, chat.

IN A CHAT: under 600px. Title, filters, a few KPIs in grid min=140, one main chart; no nested cards. Caption estimates.
- on=emit:pick:{x.name} sends a choice to you; no handler blocks. Also update the screen: on=set:sel:{x.name};emit:pick:{x.name}

colors.description: Brand colors as hex, most important first, such as ["#e4572e", "#2e86ab"]: send them only when the person, or the instructions you were given, named colors to use.
